::: {.why}
The minimum you found last night is the actual hedging decision, and it depends on the cost of trading rather than on anything in the Black-Scholes model, which is why the model has nothing to say about it.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Find the rebalancing frequency that minimises the sum of hedging error and transaction cost for a stated cost level.
- Implement a move-based hedging rule and compare it against time-based rebalancing at matched cost.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Optimise the frequency: plot total cost, defined as a stated risk aversion times the hedging error variance plus the expected transaction cost, against rebalancing frequency, at three cost levels. Read off the optimum in each case and note how strongly it depends on the cost.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Compare rules at matched cost: hedge when the delta drifts beyond a band, rather than on a schedule, and tune the band so the expected transaction cost equals that of the time-based rule. Report the hedging error of both. The band rule usually wins, because it spends its trading where the risk is.
:::
:::

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
The cost-optimal rebalancing frequency at three cost levels, and a band-based rule compared against time-based at matched cost.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
At a 5 basis point round-trip cost, how often would you rebalance a delta hedge, and what did you trade off to get there?
:::
